newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission seeks more power over air alliances.
newsitem.headline: Commission seeks more power over air alliances.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to propose rules on Wednesday that would give it clear and undisputable jurisdiction over alliances between EU and non-EU airlines.

The controversial move is aimed at avoiding future battles with national governments over the legal competence to vet deals similar to those announced last year between British Airways and AMR Corp's American Airlines, and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines and Northwest Airlines Inc.

It is not the first time the Commission has tried to gain full authority to rule on international mega-alliances involving EU-based airlines. An attempt in 1989 but ran into opposition from almost all EU states.
Commission officials and European antitrust experts think it might stand a better chance now as transatlantic deals have mushroomed raising fears that fair competition and consumers might lose out.
"There is more room for an agreement than eight years ago," one expert said, warning that the issue was still politically charged.
Whatever happens will have no bearing on the BA-American and KLM-Northwest deals as they will almost certainly have been ruled on long before any decision is taken.

Under existing regulation 3975/87 on the aplication of article 85 of the Treaty of Rome -- which bans unfair practices -- to the air transport sector, the Commission has sole jurisdiction to review alliances such as code-sharing and other agreements affecting services between EU airports.

The Commission's proposal, which will become effective on Wednesday if no reservations are raised, would extend the regulation to deals between EU and non-EU airline companies. It requires a qualified majority to become law.

In the absence of such clear-cut rules, the Commission used articles 85 and 89 of the treaty together with the air transport regulation to assert its power to investigate the proposed transatlantic air deals.

That authority was strongly contested by the former British Conservative government which argued it, not the Commission, had authority to review the alliance between BA and American Airlines under article 88 of the treaty.
European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has openly and repeatedly criticised the deal saying that it would eliminate competition on many key routes between Britain and the United States.

Van Miert also recently said that the revision of the air transport regulation was consistent with EU transport ministers' decision last year to give the Commission a much-awaited mandate to negotiate an open-skies agreement with the United States.
"One must draw the consequences and propose to the Council (of ministers) to extend the scope of the regulation to services with third countries," he told the European Parliament in February.
The battle of competences does not affect mergers and takeovers, irrespective of whether or not they involve non-EU airlines, where the Commission is the sole master.
